gaps.note: telco.com publishes data sheets only; its support page says hardware documentation is on a support portal behind a login, whose contact is on telco.com/support. The one public Telco Systems installation guide (T-Marc 3306, MN100280) is for another product. Searched: the telco.com media library (120 PDFs), every product and knowledge-centre page, and the Wayback index of telco.com PDFs.
gaps.wanted: the TM-8106 / T-Metro 8106 hardware installation guide, from the BATM support portal.

gaps.note: Block origins are the stencil's. The two vendor fronts disagree with it differently: this face's near-square 2022 front (1.8 px/mm) spreads everything about 2% outward from the left - the SFP+ blocks about 2.2 mm out on each side, the module's fourth QSFP28 cage 4.8 mm right of the stencil's - while the yaw-corrected 2021 TM-8104 render disagrees with its own stencil within -3.0 to +0.4 mm with no pattern. Neither resolves better than 2-3 mm, so the stencil stands.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing, or a square-on photograph at 4 px/mm or better.

gaps.note: No image held shows the rear. The data sheets say the fans are hot-swappable and order them as TM810x-FAN, and NetBox lists four fan bays, so the rear almost certainly holds them; where, and whether it carries a ground point or anything else, is not known.
gaps.wanted: a square-on photograph of the rear, or the installation guide's rear view.

gaps.note: No data sheet states the airflow direction. NetBox gives front-to-rear, which is a community reading with no cited source, so chassis.airflow is left unset.
The TM810x-OAM "Full FPGA Expansion Module for Base System" (ordering tables, 2025) and NetBox's "OAM Expansion Bay" have no visible opening on the front; it is presumably internal. Not drawn.
gaps.wanted: the installation guide, or a photograph of the chassis with its lid off.

gaps.note: The 2025 data sheet's ordering table gives TM8106-2QS-O-2XX the description "TM810x Expansion Module With 48x1G/10G" - the 48-port module's own line, copied - while its feature table lists the base as 2 x QSFP28 + 16 x SFP+. The configurations follow the SKU names and the feature table (2QS = the bare base, 2QS-64 = with the 48-port module, 6QS = with the QSFP28 module); no part number is attached while the table contradicts itself.

chassis.note: 2RU x 436.9 x 88.5 x 350 deep. The depth is the data sheet's (13.7 in, 350 mm). The face is the stencil's: its body between the ear folds is 165.1 units = 436.8 mm and its height 33.5 units = 88.6 mm at the stencil's 1:10, and its outline with ears is 482.9 mm - the 19-inch face, which is what fixes the scale. Two readings off the vendor's renders corroborate it: the TM-8104's 2021 render (8104-02.png, 3622 px) gives a body of 439.5 and a face of 87.8 mm, and the 2022 TM-8106 front (8106.jpg) a face aspect of 4.955, i.e. 88.8 on a 440 body. The render is yawed a little (its SFP pitch slides 14.60 -> 14.41 -> 14.34 left to right), which is why its 439.5 is not preferred over the stencil. Recorded as estimated because a stencil is a diagram symbol and no mechanical drawing is held.

chassis-height-in-the-data-sheet.note: The TM-8106 data sheet prints, as every TM-8104 edition does, "2RU H x 19'W x 13.7'D (133.35 x 482 x 350mm)". 133.35 mm is exactly THREE rack units (3 x 44.45); 2RU is 88.9. The stencil (88.6), the TM-8104's 2021 render (87.8), this box's 2022 front (88.8) and NetBox's TM-8104 (u_height 2.0) all say 2RU, so the millimetre figure is a transcription slip and 88.5 is drawn. The 482 is the 19-inch face with its ears, not the body.

ears.note: Not drawn. The stencil's ear folds are at 8.8 and 173.9 units, 23.3 mm of ear either side of the body. The data sheets order the brackets separately (TM810x-BRKT-19IN or -23IN, "Ear Side TM810x Rack Mount Brackets").

exp-slot.note: One full-width expansion slot, printed as slot 2 ("1/2/x" on the 48-port module, 1/2/1 ... 1/5/1 on the QSFP28 module). The data sheets list the two modules it takes, TM810x-48SFP+ and TM810x-4QSFP28; its size is the stencil's empty slot.

fans.note: Data sheets: "Fan: Load sharing, speed controlled, hot-swappable", orderable as TM810x-FAN. NetBox lists four fan bays on the TM-8104, whose chassis this is. Nothing held shows where they are, so no fan is drawn (see the rear-and-fans gap).

front-layout.note: Every feature is placed from the stencil master's own vector paths, extracted to chassis millimetres (x = (unit - 8.8) x 2.6458), and then checked against the 2021 render at matched scale - the chassis, supplies, slot, vent and CLI/OOB stack are the TM-8104's and were checked on it - and this face's own base board (two SFP+ blocks of 4 columns, the two QSFP28 cages and their lane lamps) against the 2022 8106 front. Every feature is present in both and in the same order. POSITIONS AGREE TO ABOUT 2.5 MM AND NO BETTER, and that is the render's limit, not the stencil's error: the render is yawed (its lamp pitch slides 14.60 -> 14.41 -> 14.34 across three identical blocks), and after integrating a local scale fitted to that slide its features sit within -3.0 (ToD shell) to +0.4 (base block B) of the stencil with no consistent pattern, and its body comes out 434.6 against 436.85. The in-block pitch, which both sources resolve well, agrees to 0.05 mm. See the block-spacing gap.

jack-lamps.note: L76 STANDS IN THE BASELINE ON PURPOSE, not waived (the waiver cap is for rules with no device-level fix). the console jack here IS lamped, so the lamped part is the right one. At 4x on the 2021 render (telco.com 2021/01/8104-02.png, 5.9 px/mm) the TM-8104's two RJ45 stacks - ToD over E1/T1 and CLI over OOB - show a bright lamp window in each outer corner of each jack, the top corners of the upper jack and the bottom corners of the lower, set in the jack housing rather than beside it; the stencil draws the same four green windows on every jack, and draws this face's CLI / OOB stack identically. docs/rj45-family-design.md's rule is that a console or timing jack carries no lamps, which is true of most boxes and not of this one. Revisit if a closer photograph shows the CLI windows are blanks.

jack-orientation.note: The CLI/OOB stack puts its lamp windows on the OUTER corners - the top corners of the upper jack and the bottom corners of the lower - in the stencil, and the TM-8104's identical stack does in the 2021 render's highlights. common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 draws its lamps on the keyway side and is keyway-down unrotated, so the upper jack is turned 180 and the lower is not.

lamps.note: One up and one down arrow lamp per SFP+ column in the pale strip between the rows (common/led-arrow@1) and four lane dots over each QSFP28, as the 2022 front and the stencil both draw. PWR, CPU1, CPU2 and FAN beside the CLI/OOB stack are common/led-dot@1 on the stencil's 2.6 mm lamps - the nearest library part, 2.0 mm, is used at the measured centres rather than a 4 mm lamp at a wrong pitch. The stencil colours FAN red and the rest green; no document says what any lamp's states mean.

logos.note: THIS FACE CARRIES NO LOGO MARK: the 2022 front prints a plain TELCO SYSTEMS wordmark over T-METRO 8106 at the base board's left, both drawn as text; there is no swirl to reserve a zone for (the TM-8104's face carries one).

model.note: TM-8106 data sheet (telco.com 2025/12), "TM-8106 Modular 1.2Tbps Service Demarcation Device (SDD)"; the 2022 editions (not held) and the stencil call it the T-Metro 8106, which is what the faceplate prints.

port-numbering.note: Legends read off the 2022 front and the stencil, which agree: the QSFP28 cages are 1/1/1 and 1/1/2, and the SFP+ columns print "3▲▼4" ... "9▲▼10" left and "11▲▼12" ... "17▲▼18" right under their blocks, "1/1/x" at each block's foot - so the SFP+ ports continue the slot-1 numbering after the two QSFP28 and run 3 to 18. The sfp-plus group therefore places its ports at rel-pos 3-18, not 1-16.

ports.note: std/sfp-ganged@1 centred on each stencil cage opening (13.91 x 9.68): upper row y 55.58, lower 71.49, columns at x 110.08 ... 152.9 and 327.04 ... 369.86, a 14.26-14.3 pitch. common/qsfp-cage@3 centred on the stencil's two 20.27 x 9.68 QSFP28 openings at x 213.35 and 260.24, y 71.79, each under four common/led-dot@1 on its 2.07 mm lane dots at y 67.63 - the 2022 front shows the same four dots above each cage. The stencil's pitch agrees with the 2021 render's two undistorted blocks (14.34, 14.41) and not with the registry's touching 14.25, so these cages stand a tenth of a millimetre apart. Odd ports above, even below; the lower row is turned 180 so both rows' lips face the lamp strip.

power.note: "Max power consumption: 400W", unqualified by configuration or ambient in the TM-8106 data sheet, as in all five TM-8104 editions - filed as the chassis maximum. No supply rating and no per-module figure is published anywhere held.

psu-bays.note: Two bays at the stencil's supply faces, 50.91 x 39.43 at y 3.9 and 45.4, labelled PS1 and PS2 reading bottom to top beside them. The data sheets: "Dual redundant, hot-swappable AC or DC 24/-48VDC".

shells.note: The silver shell around the RJ45 stack, the metal frame of each SFP+ block and the bright bezel of each QSFP28 cage are panel decor at the stencil's outlines (17.14 x 26.98, 58.16 x 27.0, 21.61 x 10.72); the 2022 front shows all three as bright metal against the black panel.

sources.note: The 2025 TM-8106 data sheet, the NetZoom stencil Telco-TM810x-04-30-2024.VSS (masters TM8106 (CF), TM810x-48SFP+, TM810x-4QSFP28), 14 vendor renders of the 8106 from the telco.com media library - among them the near-square 2022 front (8106.jpg) and one with the expansion slot empty (T-Metro-8106-HL-3.png) - and everything held for the TM-8104, whose chassis this is. NetBox has no TM-8106 entry. NO INSTALLATION GUIDE IS PUBLIC - telco.com routes hardware manuals to a support portal behind a login (see the install-guide gap).

vent.note: The perforated strip between the slot and the base board, y 41.2-48.4 across x 70.3-425.1 between the two chassis screws, from the stencil; the 2021 render shows it as two staggered rows of hexagonal holes. Hole pitch and cavity depth are not measured.
